title: Private Upgrade Autopilot Controller and Migration Safety Playbook
creator: Avery Chen
description: Design and implement an autonomous upgrade controller (Upgrade Autopilot) for Redwood Private that safely executes version upgrades and data migrations in VPC/on-prem deployments. The controller must be able to run preflight checks, perform staged schema/data transformations, coordinate node/drain operations, and enforce configurable rollout gates (canary percentage, health windows, crash thresholds). Deliver a tested operator, CI pipelines, a customer-facing runbook, and dashboards that show per-customer upgrade progress and SLO impact.
acceptance_criteria: Upgrade Autopilot operator deployed to test clusters and can run a full minor-version upgrade without manual intervention when configured (canary -> ramp -> finish).
Migrations are split into discrete, idempotent steps with built-in dry-run and forward/backward compatibility checks and can be rolled back if any step fails the health gate.
Rollout gates support at least: canary percentage, time-based hold, service-level health checks, and automatic rollback thresholds configurable per-release channel (stable/lts/edge).
Operator emits events to the Console and exposes an API for the Console to show upgrade state, per-step progress, and historic run logs for audits.
A customer-facing runbook (Confluence) and an internal runbook (runbook note + Slack escalation play) exist and are validated via a fire-drill in the staging environment.
E2E test suite in CI validates schema-migration semantics, canary rollout behavior, and rollback on injected failures. Tests run on simulated on-prem clusters (k3s) as part of the release pipeline.
Metrics and dashboards (Prometheus/Grafana and Console) show pre/post-upgrade token latency, failure rate, and resource cost deltas; alerts fire when regressions cross thresholds.
Documentation for customers describing LTS channels, recommended upgrade windows, and how to opt into or defer Autopilot upgrades is published.
steps: Prototype operator CRD: UpgradePlan with ordered MigrationSteps, healthChecks, and rolloutPolicy fields.
Implement idempotent MigrationRunner that sequences steps with dry-run mode and transaction boundaries for DB changes.
Build preflight verifier: validate compatibility matrix between current runtime, model artifacts, and migration step assumptions.
Create canary controller: route small portion of traffic to upgraded nodes and evaluate configured health probes before ramping.
Integrate with Console: event stream, per-tenant progress visualization, and manual pause/resume controls.
Add CI jobs: synthetic workload generation, chaos injection for rollback validation, and migration smoke tests on artifact snapshots.
Author customer and internal runbooks, and schedule a staged adoption pilot with 2 enterprise customers.
Run staged rollouts in staging, collect metrics, refine thresholds, and harden rollback fast-paths.
Ship operator and release notes in private-upgrades-2026.03 and coordinate SRE on-call rotation for first 72-hour upgrades.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Long-running DB migrations cause tail latency spikes. Mitigation: split migrations into smaller steps, use background copy with cutover window, and enforce per-step timeout and max-concurrent-migrations config.
Risk: Incompatible model artifacts cause inference regressions after upgrade. Mitigation: preflight artifact signature checks and a golden-sample regression test run before canary ramp.

Risk: Operator bug leads to partial upgrades across nodes. Mitigation: design operator to be level-based (desired state) and idempotent; include a reconciliation audit that can force a coordinated rollback.
Risk: Customer network constraints prevent image pulls. Mitigation: provide an air-gapped bundle with tarball images and an offline preflight that validates expected images and checksums.
Risk: Insider misconfiguration triggers a destructive migration. Mitigation: RBAC guardrails, review approvals in Console, and optional human-in-the-loop gate for critical migrations.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Avery Chen: Initial draft. Spike identified two approaches: (A) controller-driven sequential migrations with built-in rollback, (B) CI-driven migration orchestration. Prefer (A) for better customer observability and in-cluster recovery.

2026-03-01 - SRE (R. Gomez): Observability hooks need to include per-step spans and tokenized cost deltas. Added proposal for metrics in PR #712 on GitHub (https://github.com/redwood-inference/upgrade-operator/pull/712).
